solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique after crossings); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

indicators.note: travelling suggests the letters of salesmen move about into a new order

explanation.surface: Door-to-door salesmen going about their rounds without anyone knowing who they are.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone unknown has no name anyone recognises, so is anonymous.

parts.note: CON is the abbreviation for Conservative, the party of the Tories
a standard is a flag or banner
a quota is an allotted share, a ration

explanation.surface: A political row about a Conservative's fixed standard allocation, pictured as a blaze.
explanation.definitionFit: A conflagration is a large, destructive blaze, a synonym for a big fire.

indicators.note: reportedly signals a word heard said rather than written

parts.note: dark as a noun is night-time, night

explanation.surface: A news report about some shadowy item.
explanation.walkthrough: 'piece' is a chess piece; the word said for 'dark' is spelt with a silent K.
explanation.definitionFit: The knight is one of the chessmen, a piece in the game of chess.

indicators.note: holding means the reversed word wraps round the next piece
in a down clue, up means the word is read from bottom to top, backwards

parts.note: the back of something is its rear
PI, short for pious, is crossword shorthand for good

explanation.surface: An instruction to reverse while carrying a fine blade.
explanation.walkthrough: PI for 'good' is a crossword convention (pious). In a down clue 'up' reads REAR upwards as RAER.
explanation.definitionFit: A rapier is a long, thin, pointed duelling blade, a kind of sword.

clue.text: Finally improve, or go round the bend?

definitions.meaning: an idiom for at last beginning to recover
literally, to ... is to go round a bend in the road

explanation.surface: A wry question: does getting better mean going mad?
explanation.walkthrough: 'go round the bend' also suggests going crazy, but here it is taken literally.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes passing the critical point of an illness or crisis and starting to get better.

definitions.meaning: freshly reported happenings, as in a bulletin
the four compass points together, written as their initial letters, spell the word

explanation.surface: A bulletin reaching every corner of the country.
explanation.walkthrough: The second half is cryptic: north, east, west and south abbreviate to N, E, W, S, playing on the fanciful idea that news comes from all directions.
explanation.definitionFit: News is fresh information that is reported, as in a bulletin or paper.

definitions.meaning: to abandon someone, desert them, on an island

explanation.walkthrough: 'Desert' reads as sandy wasteland but is the verb to abandon.
explanation.definitionFit: Marooning abandons a person somewhere remote; maroon is also a dark red colour.

clue.text: Charm in a hybrid tree, originally

parts.note: a mule is a hybrid, the offspring of a donkey and a horse

indicators.note: originally points to the opening letter of the word tree

explanation.surface: A good-luck token found in a cross-bred tree.
explanation.definitionFit: An amulet is a lucky trinket worn to ward off harm, a charm.

definitions.meaning: muscle or brawn, as in a beefy person
slang for a grievance or complaint

explanation.definitionFit: Beef is informal for muscular strength and also slang for a grumble.

indicators.note: mixed says the letters of blessing are stirred into a new order

explanation.surface: Smooth talk is a gift with downsides, a mixed blessing.
explanation.definitionFit: Glibness is fluent but shallow talk, the trait of being silver-tongued.

clue.text: Stoppered vessel, vessel secured by stop!

indicators.note: secured by means held within the word that follows

parts.note: to deter is to stop or discourage
a can is a container, a vessel

explanation.surface: A description of a wine bottle with its stopper, ending in an exclamation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'vessel' appears twice: once inside the definition, once as wordplay. 'stop!' reads as a command but is the verb meaning discourage.
explanation.definitionFit: A decanter is a glass bottle with a stopper used for serving wine.

clue.text: Look at yours truly when speaking

indicators.note: when speaking signals that the word is heard aloud, not spelt

parts.note: yours truly is a jokey way of saying me, I

explanation.surface: An invitation to regard the speaker while they talk.
explanation.definitionFit: To eye something is to look at it closely, a verb synonym.

definitions.meaning: the joint in a horse's hind leg

explanation.walkthrough: 'White' looks like a colour describing the horse, but it is a wine.
explanation.definitionFit: Hock is a white Rhine wine and also a leg joint of a horse.

parts.note: a crack is a try, an attempt
a pot is a sum of prize money, or a trophy cup

explanation.surface: A mad bid to win an award.
explanation.definitionFit: Crackpot as an adjective means eccentric or mad, synonymous with crazy.

clue.text: Employer held back by chores, unfortunately

indicators.note: back says those concealed letters are then read in reverse order
held means the letters sit inside the words chores unfortunately

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A boss slowed down by tedious household tasks.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft gave the concealment no signal; 'held' signals it and 'back' the reversal, with 'by' a link. RESU spans choRES Unfortunately.
explanation.definitionFit: A user is one who employs something, puts it to use.

clue.text: Male in fancy red coat, US politician

indicators.note: in places the abbreviation inside the rearranged letters
fancy suggests the letters of red coat are elaborately rearranged

explanation.surface: A man in a showy scarlet jacket, who turns out to be an American politician.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fancy' turns REDCOAT into DEOCRAT, and 'in' puts M inside it. 'Red coat' may suggest a British soldier, but it is only letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A Democrat is a member of one of the two main parties in the United States.

clue.text: Biblical character in deal that's dodgy

indicators.note: dodgy says the letters of in deal are not to be trusted in their order

explanation.surface: A figure from scripture caught up in a shady deal.
explanation.definitionFit: Daniel is a prophet in the Old Testament, thrown into the lions' den.

clue.text: Pole saving company, is that lucky?

indicators.note: saving here means keeping the next piece safe inside

parts.note: a mast is a tall pole

explanation.surface: A Polish person rescuing a firm, with a question about luck.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pole' looks like a Polish person but is a post.
explanation.definitionFit: A mascot is a person, animal or object thought to bring good luck.

clue.text: Battle, as things going to pieces

indicators.note: going to pieces says the letters of as things fall apart and regroup

explanation.surface: A fight in which everything falls apart.
explanation.walkthrough: The Battle of Hastings in 1066 was the Norman conquest of England.
explanation.definitionFit: Hastings is the name of the famous 1066 battle in which William the Conqueror won England.

indicators.note: initially missing means the word loses its opening letter

explanation.surface: Deals without their opening lines, written up as a volume.
explanation.definitionFit: Acts of the Apostles is a book of the New Testament, known simply as Acts.

definitions.meaning: a man of loose morals, a libertine
a toothed tool for gathering leaves

explanation.definitionFit: Rake names both a debauched man about town and a long-handled toothed implement.

indicators.note: dancing sets the letters of a mo the jigging into a new order

explanation.surface: A promise that the dancing will start shortly.
explanation.definitionFit: Being in means being present at your house, not out.

indicators.note: destroying says the word Borneo is broken up and rebuilt

explanation.surface: A monarch on stage laying waste to an island.
explanation.definitionFit: Oberon is king of the fairies in Shakespeare's A Midsummer Night's Dream.
